title: The component plan says which keys, flags and coordinate rule each slice uses
goal: A plan for building components already exists and says what a component is, how copies stay linked, and in what order the pieces get built. Three things it does not say would each be guessed differently by whoever builds next: where a piece inside a group thinks it is, which menu items and keyboard shortcuts each step adds, and which switch in the Experiments window turns each step on. Fill those in so the ladder is built one way.
notes:
RETARGETED by the 2026-09-03 retriage. The original task asked for a new page, docs/design/next-components.md. While it sat in the queue, docs/design/ui-building.md was written and it already covers the IA (one tree, Library as a panel group, main/instance/override/variant, styles), the nine step order of work, the deferred list and the user decisions. Writing a second page now would be two sources of truth for the same ladder, so this task shrank to the three gaps that page has: no coordinate rule, no menu items or shortcuts, no flag names.

The coordinate rule is the one that has to be settled first, because layers-can-hold-layers is built straight after this and encodes it. The recommendation already written into that task is that a child frame is relative to its parent, which is what an instance needs: a main is placed at many spots and its children cannot each carry canvas coordinates.

Photoshop parity on the keys (user preference): Command G groups, Shift Command G ungroups. Option Command K for Make Component is what the component task assumes.

Objective: ui-components (staged now, under the focus). It is the spec the rest of the ladder is built from, and it earns its place by stopping four later slices from each inventing a different answer.
acceptance: docs/design/ui-building.md states whether a layer inside a group stores its position against its parent or against the whole picture, and why, in one short section
It lists, per step in The order of work, the menu items and keyboard shortcuts that step adds, using the Photoshop shortcut where one exists
It names the feature flag each step ships behind, and whether that flag is on by default in Next
It says what the first version deliberately does not do, so later work is not judged against a promise nobody made
No second component page is written: everything lands in the existing document

log.note: Adversarial pass on the plan before writing. Three collisions the ladder tasks would each have guessed: (1) a group whose origin follows the union of its children silently rewrites every sibling number each time you draw, so the origin is set once at group time and then holds still; (2) double click already means edit this text and edit this arrow caption, so entering a group needs a rule that covers all three, and it is descend one level; (3) Escape already runs a priority order on the canvas, so stepping out of a group has to slot into it rather than be added on top. None of these has a visible consequence worth a decision card: each has one sound answer, so they are decided in the doc and noted here.

Wrote three new sections into docs/design/ui-building.md, no second page. A layer position is stored against its parent (with translation-only groups, a fixed group origin, reparenting rewrites, Position and Size fields in parent space, and old flat documents decoding unchanged). The menu items and keys each step adds (a per-step table keyed on The order of work, plus where each row sits, why each key was chosen, and the two canvas gestures). The flag each step ships behind (six Next-only flags, all on by default, with what turning each off restores and the prerequisite rule).

Keys settled: Command G group and Shift Command G ungroup (Photoshop parity, the user preference); F for the frame tool, Option Command K make component, Option Command B detach (design tool parity, Photoshop has no equivalent command); Frame Selection and the Library toggle deliberately get no key, since Option Command G is Photoshops clipping mask and Option Command L is already Show Layers. Checked against every shortcut in EditorCommands.swift and every tool key in Tools.swift: no collisions.

Flags settled: next-layer-groups, next-frames, next-library, next-components, next-styles, next-starter-components. All Next only, all on by default, matching every other Next flag in FeatureCatalog. The model and the renderer are never flagged, so turning a flag off removes a way in and never a documents contents.

Also added a fourth section, What the first version deliberately does not do (eleven limits), and a note in The order of work that step 8 styles is built before step 7 built-ins. Numbering left alone on purpose: the queue tasks quote D7 and D8, so swapping them would invert every reference.
Scripts/test.sh green, 1533 tests. Docs only change, so no build or app run and no audit: an audit is for something a person can try, and a spec page is not.

Three missing answers written into docs/design/ui-building.md (no second page): the coordinate rule (a layer stores its position against its parent, groups translate only, the group origin holds still), a per-step table of menu items and keys (Command G / Shift Command G for group and ungroup per Photoshop parity, F, Option Command K, Option Command B where Photoshop has no equivalent, no key for Frame Selection or the Library toggle), and the six Next-only flags each step ships behind, all on by default. Plus a section on what the first version deliberately does not do, and the two canvas gestures (double click descends, Escape comes back out) since both keys were already taken. Verified: every key checked against EditorCommands.swift and Tools.swift for collisions, flag defaults checked against FeatureCatalog. Scripts/test.sh green, 1533 tests. Committed 263ab31 and pushed.
